messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Project overlap
parts:
Hi all,

What's the policy on overlapping proposals? By my count there are now
at least 12 serious proposals related to finance/time series. I
realise that these cover a number of different topics, but I worry a
little that other fields are getting lost in the mix.

It may be also a little biased, but I wonder why the finance community
can't pay for these directly? The cost of a google summer of code
student is substantially less than an in person internship (about
five-fold compared to some of the students I've talked to), and the
finance community does have a lot of money...

Hadley

--
Assistant Professor / Dobelman Family Junior Chair
Department of Statistics / Rice University
http://had.co.nz/

On Tue, 2012-04-10 at 09:25 -0500, Hadley Wickham wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> What's the policy on overlapping proposals? By my count there are now
> at least 12 serious proposals related to finance/time series. I
> realise that these cover a number of different topics, but I worry a
> little that other fields are getting lost in the mix.
>
> It may be also a little biased, but I wonder why the finance community
> can't pay for these directly? The cost of a google summer of code
> student is substantially less than an in person internship (about
> five-fold compared to some of the students I've talked to), and the
> finance community does have a lot of money...

We will, as has been the policy in the past, only accept one for each
non-overlapping project.

The Finance projects you mention received over half of the student
submissions, almost all from students unknown to the project mentors. I
can assure you that they will not take half the slots.

As in previous years, and per Google policy, the top rated proposals
marked 'Accept' will get the slots.
